places.now: Alps; point is the summit of Mont Blanc
places.reason: Range-level representative point at Mont Blanc, the highest and best-known peak, near Chamonix and Frankenstein's journey to Chamonix and Montanvert.

places.now: Jura Mountains; point is near the Jura crest above Geneva (Crêt de la Neige area is slightly west)
places.reason: The Jura range lies northwest of Lake Geneva; the point is on the crest visible from Geneva, with the highest peak Crêt de la Neige at about 46.27, 5.94.

places.now: Rhine; point is the middle Rhine near Koblenz
places.reason: Frankenstein and Clerval travel down the Rhine from Strasbourg/Mannheim to Cologne, so the stretch near Koblenz and the Rhine gorge is representative.
Salève is the limestone ridge just south of Geneva, visible from Lake Geneva; the point is near its summit (Grand Piton about 1,379 m).

places.now: Geographic North Pole, in the Arctic Ocean
places.reason: The novel's 'pole' is the geographic North Pole, which Walton hopes to reach; the gazetteer's Alaska town is a modern namesake.
Region-level point in the northwest Highlands; Victor goes to a remote Orkney island, but 'northern highlands' is a vague region so the point is only representative.
The large lake on the Swiss-French border near Geneva, where the Frankensteins' home at Belrive and Plainpalais lies on the south shore; the point is mid-lake.
Holland proper corresponds to the provinces of North and South Holland; the point is near Leiden/The Hague on the western coast.

places.now: Aconcagua, the highest peak of the Andes
places.reason: The 'highest peak of the Andes' in Clerval's wish is Aconcagua (then thought Chimborazo by some, but Aconcagua is the highest); used as the range's representative point.

places.now: Probably Liebfrauenmünster (Church of Our Lady) or Moritzkirche in Ingolstadt
places.reason: Shelley's white steeple and clock is not identified; candidates are Moritzkirche (white tower, the gazetteer's guess) or Liebfrauenmünster, so the point is only in the old town.

places.now: Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark
places.reason: The island is well known; the point is in the interior, and whalers worked the waters off its coasts.

places.now: Col du Mont-Cenis, on the French-Italian border, with Lac du Mont-Cenis
places.reason: Mont Cenis is the Alpine pass between Savoy and Piedmont used as the route from France to Italy; the gazetteer's Paris street is a modern namesake.
